summary: Embedding checksum mismatch across serving replicas causing inconsistent rerank results for identical requests
description: Issue summary: Customer AtlasSearch reports that identical rerank requests (same prompt, same document set, same model pins) intermittently return different top-K ordering when the request is routed to different serving replicas. Impact: Search quality is inconsistent for end users, observed by customer as 'search results jumping' and causing UX regressions. Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated-asia fallback disabled) in prod us-west, using models rwd-open-encoder-768 for embeddings and rwd-sim-384 for similarity scoring. Steps to reproduce: 1) Call /v1/rerank with fixed request_id and payload multiple times over a minute; 2) Force routing to different replicas by toggling header X-RW-Replica or by using the Canary routing tool in console; 3) Compare returned top-10 ordering and pairwise similarity scores. Observed behavior: In ~4% of cross-replica comparisons the returned order differs (rank flips among top-5). Cosine similarities differ by ~0.0007-0.002 in these cases. Expected behavior: Deterministic rerank ordering for identical input and pinned model version across replicas. Initial hypothesis: Replica-local embedding cache or serialization subtlety leading to binary differences (checksum mismatch) at read time causing tiny numerical differences that change ranking ties. Additional notes: No errors/5xx; tokenization and model version confirmed identical by customer; replicas show different checksum metadata for the same embedding key in internal cache store.
comments: Support (2026-03-10T10:45Z) - Aisha Patel: Opened ticket after customer provided paired rerank payloads and two trace IDs. Customer included two POST bodies and the two resulting orderings. Requested immediate triage and whether we can reproduce from console routing.

SRE (2026-03-10T12:02Z) - Miguel Ortega: I reproduced locally using the customer's payload. When routing to replica A vs B I observed cosine differences matching the customer's report. Captured binary embedding blobs from both replicas and computed checksums; hashes differ. No runtime errors logged on either replica during request window.

Engineer (2026-03-10T13:20Z) - Priya Singh: Investigation: pulled cache backend rows for the embedding keys. Replica A shows metadata header 'cs-v1' while Replica B shows 'cs-v0' for same key. Suspect a previous rollout introduced a header change that didn't perform a migration; some replicas accepted new checksum-on-write, others kept legacy write path. If read code is tolerant, differing serialization produces small fp diffs on similarity aggregator.

Support (2026-03-10T14:05Z) - Aisha Patel: Shared mitigation steps to customer: 1) pinned traffic to a single replica group as short-term workaround; 2) suggested disabling cross-replica routing for sensitive rerank endpoints. Customer applied pinned routing and reported stability increase within 15 minutes.

SRE (2026-03-11T09:30Z) - Miguel Ortega: Performed live cache validation across all replicas in dedicated pool. Found ~2.1% of embedding keys had mismatched checksum header. Executed a coordinated cache-validation job that read, reserialized, and rewrote keys to unify header to 'cs-v1' for replicas running the new writer. Job completed without errors; monitoring shows reduction in rank-flip incidents to <0.1% during sample window.

Engineer (2026-03-11T17:45Z) - Priya Singh: Root cause: rollout last week introduced a serialization header change (cs-v1) with a non-idempotent writer path. Some replicas still on older binary that wrote with cs-v0. Read path accepted both but downstream similarity aggregation had micro differences after deserialization due to alignment/endianness expectations. Fix: make serialization stable and authoritative by validating checksum on read and normalizing during read if legacy format detected.

Product (2026-03-12T08:10Z) - Jordan Lee: Proposed release plan: hotfix to normalize on-read to be merged to stable channel today, follow-up migration job to sweep remaining pools, and a small dashboard metric to alert if >0.5% keys differ. Also propose a canary rollout with 100 requests per minute for 30 minutes.

Customer (AtlasSearch) (2026-03-12T11:00Z) - Elena Moore: Confirmed pinned routing workaround reduced user complaints. We appreciate ETA on permanent fix; please advise if there will be any user visible downtime for migration.

SRE (2026-03-12T12:15Z) - Miguel Ortega: Hotfix PR created and passed unit tests (see related_github_prs). Plan to deploy to staging first, then gradual rollout to prod with migration job for cache normalization. No user-visible downtime expected; migration uses per-key rewrite and does not block reads. Scheduling deployment for 2026-03-13 02:00Z UTC (low traffic window).
workaround: Customer pinned routing to a single replica group; support triggered cache normalization job for affected dedicated pool. This removes cross-replica ordering variance until permanent fix is deployed.
next_steps: 1) Deploy hotfix patch that normalizes embedding serialization on read and enforces checksum-on-write in the writer path. 2) Run full cache migration sweep across all dedicated pools and add an automated consistency check. 3) Add dashboard alert for checksum-header drift and include in post-deployment runbook. 4) Follow up with AtlasSearch to validate on production traffic after rollout.
resolution: Workaround applied (routing pin + local normalization job). Hotfix PR merged to main and scheduled for staged rollout 2026-03-13. Pending verification from customer after rollout.
